title: RADiT: Redundancy-Aware Diffusion Transformer Acceleration Leveraging Timestep Similarity
problem: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) require multiple iterative sampling timesteps with redundant computations across consecutive steps, leading to high latency and energy consumption during inference.
motivation: DiTs have become the mainstream generative model for image and video generation; reducing computational redundancy and energy cost is critical for real-time applications.
method: RADiT detects redundancy by examining blocks of input features to find when consecutive timesteps repeat the same computation. When redundancy is found, it reuses the previous result instead of recomputing. The Dynamic Threshold Scaling Module adjusts how strict the similarity check is to preserve accuracy, while the Compress and Compare Unit identifies when input blocks are similar enough to reuse.
key_novelty: Diffusion transformers repeat computations across consecutive timesteps with similar input blocks; RADiT detects this similarity using adjustable thresholds and reuses results rather than recomputing.
contributions: 1.8x faster image generation and 1.7x faster video generation without quality loss
41% energy reduction for images, 45.5% for videos
1.67-1.76x throughput improvement with maintained output quality
primary_theme: timestep redundancy elimination for diffusion acceleration
